Bayes outbreak detection

Source: R/sep.R
bayout.Rd

The Bayes detector of surveillance::algo.bayes() (Riebler 2004; Hoehle 2007) for a series of counts: at each time t the reference counts are the w before it (acty = TRUE) and, in each of the b years before, the 2 w + 1 counts around the same time of year (freq counts per year); missing counts are left out. With s their sum and n their number, the posterior predictive distribution of the count at t under a Poisson model with a flat prior is negative binomial of size s + 0.5 and probability n / (n + 1); its 1 - alpha quantile is the upper bound, and a count above it raises an alarm. The same series may be calls for service, emergency visits or reported crimes of one kind.

Usage

bayout(x, freq = 52, b = 0, w = 6, acty = TRUE, alpha = 0.05, at = NULL)

Arguments

x

The counts: numbers from 0, NA for a missing count.

freq

The counts per year: one whole number from 1 (52 for weeks).

b

The number of past years: one whole number from 0.

w

The half-width of the window: one whole number from 0.

acty

TRUE to use the w counts just before t.

alpha

The level: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

at

NULL for every time from b freq + w + 1 on, or the times to evaluate (from 1).

Value

A data frame with one row per time: t, ub (the upper bound) and alarm (NA where the count is missing).

References

Hoehle, M. (2007). surveillance: an R package for the monitoring of infectious diseases. Computational Statistics, 22(4), 571-582. doi:10.1007/s00180-007-0074-8

Riebler, A. (2004). Empirischer Vergleich von statistischen Methoden zur Ausbruchserkennung bei Surveillance Daten. Bachelor's thesis, University of Munich.

See also

Other spatial epidemiology: bufexp(), bym2sc(), ecolrg(), evfilt(), kerexp(), lerprc(), sfrail(), spbias(), spsir()

Examples

bayout(c(3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 3, 4, 12), w = 6, at = 8)
#>   t ub alarm
#> 1 8  8  TRUE
